fact: The FDSI director general said on 8 July 2026 that RSU data have been used by the ANIES and IMF Guichet Choc Alimentaire project, by UNICEF to follow malnourished children and by SOS Villages d'Enfants for family-strengthening, and that the RSU is the single entry point of social interventions under its decree.
The FDSI director general said RSU data have already served as the beneficiary base for the ANIES and IMF Guichet Choc Alimentaire project, among other partnerships.

UNICEF's representative said the RSU report is a step towards a progressively built integrated register of persons to be interoperable with other government databases and linkable to a unique national identification number.
Decree D/2024/177 of 13 October 2024 makes the RSU the single entry point for social protection and requires partners' social protection interventions to be based on data extracted from it.
On 27 June 2024 the ANIES and FDSI directors general signed a protocol for ANIES to use secured RSU data for the IMF-financed Guichet Choc Alimentaire project, aimed at 51,259 indigent households.
